text:
Maria Chen: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm leaning toward a "mirrorless cutover" approach for canary/A-B rollouts where we avoid live traffic mirroring and instead rely on staged siphoning + probabilistic routing + fast fallback. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and proposed safety net layers.

Josh Patel: Mirrorless = no shadow traffic at all? curious what we lose vs. complexity saved.

Maria Chen: Right — no persistent shadowing. Plan: 1) short-lived siphon (0.5-2s) to validate cold-start / latency, 2) sample X% of real traffic (very small initially) with header flags, 3) realtime quality checks + latency SLO monitoring, 4) automated rollback if checkers trip.

Alex Gomez: I like minimizing IO cost. Biggest risk is unseen behavior on long-tail inputs. How do checkers catch semantic degradation?

Maria Chen: Good point. We propose two tiers: syntactic/telemetry checks (latency, error-rate, token-rate anomalies) and semantic checks (small set of golden prompts + fuzzy similarity threshold using embeddings). Semantic checks run async on 0.1% of traffic but are strict.

Sudha Rao: What about safety for stateful sessions / KV caches? If we route 2% of a user's requests to canary then back to primary, we may break coherence. Need session-affinity guard.

Josh Patel: Agree. Proposed rule: affinity buckets for "session-heavy" tenants; those get canary only if warmup success observed for that tenant (warmup = successful prefix KV primes within 30s). Otherwise exclude.

Alex Gomez: How do we implement rollback firing? Circuit breaker style?

Maria Chen: Draft config snippet for the policy: 

```yaml
policy:
  sampling: 0.02
  warmup_window_sec: 30
  telemetry_checks:
    - name: latency_p95
      threshold_ms: 1200
    - name: err_rate
      threshold_pct: 1.5
  semantic_checks:
    sampling: 0.001
    embedding_threshold: 0.82
  fallback_action: immediate_rollback
  cooldown_sec: 300
```

Josh Patel: Love the cooldown. One more: add a "graceful-fallback" option that streams a short explanatory message to client and retries on stable model rather than full hard rollback. Some apps would prefer degraded UX over sudden variant swap.

Maria Chen: Added: fallback_action can be immediate_rollback | graceful_failover. Graceful semantics: attempt local inference with cached prefix, then failover after N tokens.

Sudha Rao: Telemetry signal design: need aggregated per-tenant and per-model metrics, plus a real-time sliding window anomaly detector. Also add alerting thresholds that notify oncall before auto-rollback if anomaly confidence low.

Alex Gomez: Ops question: How does this interact with Dedicated pools? We might not be allowed to route tenants across tenants.

Maria Chen: For Dedicated -> policy will enforce model-variant co-location constraints. If tenant is on dedicated pool and canary variant isn't, fallback to graceful_failover or skip canary until variant is present.

deploy-bot: Deployment triggered for branch "mirrorless-cutover/proto" by Alex Gomez at 1749997792. Canaries: 2 nodes, sampling=0.02.

Josh Patel: Quick checklist before we iterate on RFC: (1) define golden prompt set (ops + prod owners), (2) implement embedding-based similarity service (low-cost), (3) session affinity opt-in for tenants, (4) graceful-fallback UX contract, (5) instrumentation hooks in runtime to expose warmup state.

Maria Chen: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with state machine diagrams and the affinity gating API. If no major objections, I'll file PR for the policy schema and a quick prototype for the embedding checker.

Alex Gomez: +1 from me. Can we add a small synthetic fuzz runner during canary windows to exercise long-tail? maybe run queued low-priority jobs against variant.

Sudha Rao: +1, and add a runbook addendum for oncall describing when to flip cooldown off manually.

Maria Chen: thanks all — will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
